title: Prospective observational study to investigate the long-term course of MR-guided percutaneous tumor ablation of primary or secondary liver or kidney tumors
summary:
A registry will be established to collect data on percutaneous tumor ablation for renal or liver tumors. This is a minimally invasive procedure in which a special puncture needle is inserted through the skin directly into the tumor. Various techniques can be used for the subsequent actual tumor removal: Radio- or microwaves, laser, ultrasound or electroporation, or hypothermia (cryoablation). Among these methods can be chosen - depending on the size, location and type of tumor.
The registry will help to collect and evaluate data on efficacy, safety, and long-term outcome (including survival, recurrence rate) in a standardized manner. In particular, it is hoped that the results of the study will provide guidance on the optimal indications for ablation techniques.

This is a non-interventional study, i.e. patients will be treated routinely and no study-related measures will be performed except for data collection.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

interventions.name:
Patients undergoing a tumor ablation procedure as part of their treatment using one of the following (approved) techniques:
Radiofrequency-, microwave-, lase-r or cryoablation, high-intensity focused ultrasound, electroporation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients who have clinically indicated tumor ablation for primary or secondary liver or kidney tumors.
- The indication for percutaneous tumor ablation takes place in an interdisciplinarytumor conference.
- Completion of the age of 18 and the patient's legal capacity to give consent.
- Concomitant diseases or adjuvant chemotherapy or previous therapy using transarterial chemotherapy or other ablation procedures do not constitute exclusion criteria for participation in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing or incomplete declaration of consent from the patient.
- Minor patients.
- Pregnant / breastfeeding women.
- Patients incapable of giving consent.
